project.name: Harbor
project.summary: One screen that hosts many separate trading apps side by side, with a single sign-in. The apps never talk to each other directly: everything they share, like the order you just picked, goes through a central message broker. All data is made up.

nodes.label: Desktop shell
nodes.summary: The one page people open: sign-in, the app rail, the panel layout, and the top and bottom bars around every app.

nodes.label: Shell screens
nodes.summary: The visible parts of the shell: sign-in, top bar, app rail, panel layout, app library, alerts drawer and the message log.

nodes.label: Saved workspaces
nodes.summary: Remembers which apps are open and where, and offers ready-made layouts for each role.

nodes.label: Command palette
nodes.summary: The Cmd-K search box that finds apps, workspaces and actions as you type.

nodes.label: Alert centre
nodes.summary: Collects alerts that apps raise and keeps them for the alerts drawer.

nodes.label: Trading apps
nodes.summary: Separate apps, each built and served on its own, that the shell shows inside locked-down frames.

nodes.label: Pre-Trade
nodes.summary: Estimates what an order will cost and recommends how to trade it.

nodes.label: FX Execution
nodes.summary: The trade ticket: asks banks for quotes or runs an algorithm, then books the fill.

nodes.label: Post-Trade
nodes.summary: Matches finished trades and shows the ones that need attention.

nodes.label: Trade cost analysis
nodes.summary: Charts how well each trade was done compared with the market.

nodes.label: Cash
nodes.summary: A money-market fund portal that checks each investment against policy.

nodes.label: Payments
nodes.summary: Cross-border payments with a locked rate and a second person to approve.

nodes.label: Research
nodes.summary: A research reader that filters notes by currency pair.

nodes.label: Partner News
nodes.summary: Pretends to be an outside company's app, with its own look, to prove an outsider can plug in.

nodes.label: Interop Probe
nodes.summary: A developer tool for sending and watching messages, served from two addresses.

nodes.label: Message broker
nodes.summary: The only way apps share anything: it checks who sent each message, whether they're allowed, and passes it on.

nodes.label: Broker
nodes.summary: Runs inside the shell, routes messages between apps and keeps a log of them.

nodes.label: App connector
nodes.summary: What each app calls to send and receive messages through the broker.

nodes.label: App starter kit
nodes.summary: Shared start-up code every app uses: connect, load the user, show loading and error states.

nodes.label: Tiles and blotter
nodes.summary: Smaller pieces that run inside the shell itself: the order blotter, summary tiles and developer tools.

nodes.label: Design system
nodes.summary: Shared colours, spacing and components so every app looks the same.

nodes.label: Colours and spacing
nodes.summary: The fixed set of colours, sizes and spacing every screen uses.

nodes.label: Shared components
nodes.summary: Buttons, grids, dialogs, trading widgets and number formatting.

nodes.label: Pretend market data
nodes.summary: Makes up orders, prices and services from a seed, so every app shows the same numbers.

nodes.label: Message rules
nodes.summary: Defines the shape of every message, user, app listing and saved workspace, and rejects anything that doesn't fit.

nodes.label: Tests
nodes.summary: Automatic checks: small checks beside the code and full click-through tests of the main trading loop.

nodes.label: Build setup
nodes.summary: Settings for building, testing and checking the code, and the script that prepares the hosted copy.

nodes.label: Browser storage
nodes.summary: The browser's own storage, used to remember the signed-in user, workspaces and pending payments.

nodes.label: Dockview
nodes.summary: The library that draws the draggable, dockable panels.

nodes.label: AG Grid
nodes.summary: The library behind the data tables.

links.desc: Apps run in separate frames, so the connector sends every request to the broker as a browser message, and the broker checks where it came from before accepting it.
The panel layout loads each app from its own address inside a locked-down frame, using the list of apps the shell fetches at start-up.
Payments are the one thing kept across reloads, because approval needs a second user to sign in.

flows.title: From order to trade
flows.description: The trader's main loop: pick an order, see its cost, trade it, and watch it reach the review apps.

steps.note: The trader clicks the 'Orders awaiting execution' tile.
The blotter narrows to those orders, and the trader selects one. The blotter announces the selected order.
The broker checks the message is valid and passes it to every app on the same channel.
Pre-Trade shows the expected cost and recommends asking banks for quotes.
'Execute via RFQ' opens FX Execution with the ticket already filled in. The trader accepts the best quote.
The new trade is announced to everyone through the broker.
Trade cost analysis shows the trade straight away, and Post-Trade matches it a few seconds later.

tour.title: What Harbor is
tour.note: One screen that holds many trading apps at once. You sign in once and every app knows who you are.

tour.title: The apps
tour.note: Each app is built separately and shown in its own locked-down frame. They can't see each other.

tour.title: How they talk
tour.note: Everything the apps share goes through the broker, which checks who's asking and whether they're allowed.

tour.title: The rules for messages
tour.note: Every message has to match a known shape, or it's thrown away before it reaches anyone.

tour.title: Where the numbers come from
tour.note: There is no real server. The data is made up from a seed, so every app shows the same prices.

tour.title: Where the trading loop starts
tour.note: The order blotter is where a trader picks an order, and that choice ripples out to the other apps.

tasks.title: Host Harbor on Firebase
tasks.summary: Every Harbor app now builds under one web address so the whole desktop can be hosted on Firebase and opened from the File Gallery. The shell works out app addresses relative to where it's hosted.

items.note: New: builds every app into one folder with an app list that uses relative addresses, which is what lets Harbor be hosted at a single address.
Now turns the relative app addresses in the hosted app list into full ones at start-up, so the security checks still know each app's real address.
Opens popped-out panels from a page relative to where the shell is hosted, rather than the site root.
